aboutH2: Andy’s House: English-Language Addiction Treatment in Lachine, Montreal
intro: Andy’s House is a drug and alcohol rehab center founded and operated by people in long-term recovery and caring professionals. They offer various programs such as residential, intensive outpatient (IOP), and aftercare that aim to help clients overcome addiction and achieve lasting recovery. Their treatment approach is based on the Minnesota 12-Step model, which involves acknowledging powerlessness, surrendering to a higher power, and making amends. Additionally, they provide therapies such as psychoeducational groups, cognitive behavioral groups, and problem-solving groups to help clients understand and overcome their addiction triggers.

Andy’s House offers interpersonal processes approach coaching to help clients better understand their social roles and relationship dynamics. This therapy aims to promote change and healing by empowering clients to develop better communication skills, emotional regulation, and relationship building. They work closely with clients to identify the underlying causes of their addiction, including unresolved traumas, behavioral patterns, or negative belief systems that affect their relationships.

pillars.title: The Andy’s House Facility
pillars.body: The Andy’s House facility provides a comfortable and peaceful environment that facilitates recovery. The rehab is located just a 5-minute walk from the St Lawrence River and features an old Victorian mansion with outdoor space and a pool in the backyard. The facility is deliberately set up to make residents feel welcomed and at home. Additionally, Andy’s House provides a well-rounded schedule for clients that includes holistic and alternative therapies such as art therapy, cinema therapy, physical fitness, daily journaling, yoga, and recreational therapy. They also offer evidence-based therapies to help clients overcome addiction.

pillars.title: Andy’s House Aftercare Program
pillars.body: Andy’s House offers a 2-year aftercare program that allows clients to stay connected with their support network and discuss their week in recovery. This program provides a structured environment that helps clients transition back to their normal life and maintain their sobriety. Aftercare includes group meetings, individual therapy, and case management services to ensure clients have the necessary resources to stay on track. Family support is also an open-ended service provided regardless of whether a client is still a part of the program or has graduated. Weekly family support groups are available to all family members seeking guidance and support.

pillars.title: Started by People Who Went Through Treatment Themselves
pillars.body: Andy’s House is named after director Mike Weston’s brother Andy, who died in 1998 at 22. Mike went through a 90-day program himself in 1997. In 2015 he became a co-owner of the centre with Glenn Short and Isobel Williams, and that August they moved into the current house in Lachine. Glenn is now clinical director and a CACCF member. Dr. David Luckow, a family physician and diplomate of the American Board of Addiction Medicine, is the addictions physician, and Tara Reymond, a psychotherapist licensed with the Ordre des psychologues du Québec, sees residents one to one. Case managers, an art therapist and a yoga instructor make up the rest of the team.

overview: At Andy’s House, clients can expect a warm and supportive environment, where they can feel confident that their recovery is top priority. The skilled staff and comprehensive program is designed to address all aspects of addiction and encourage the path to recovery. The team at Andy’s House understands that each journey is unique, which is why they tailor their treatments to meet individual needs. From the cozy accommodations to the highly effective therapies, everything is set up to support the client’s healing journey. If addiction has taken hold of your life or that of a loved one, consider reaching out to Andy’s House for the compassionate care and supportive environment needed for recovery.

location.heading: Andy’s House in Lachine, Quebec
location.intro: Andy’s House is in Lachine, a borough on the west end of the Island of Montreal, a block from the Lachine waterfront on Lac Saint-Louis and close to Highway 20. Downtown Montreal is about 20 minutes away by car, Dorval and the rest of the West Island about 10 to 15 minutes, Laval and Longueuil roughly 30 minutes, Ottawa about 2 hours and Quebec City about 3 hours.

faqIntro: Answers come from the centre's listing and its own website. Still unsure? Call, it's free and confidential.

faqs.q: How much does Andy’s House cost?
faqs.a: Recovery.com lists an estimated private-pay rate of $29,000 or more for a residential stay of 35 days or longer. Andy’s House does not post prices on its own site and asks you to contact the director for current fees. The centre says the cost covers all programming, with personal items and medication extra, and financing is available through Medicard and Crédit Médical.

faqs.q: How long are the programs at Andy’s House?
faqs.a: Andy’s House runs a 90-day residential program and a shorter 30-day residential program. The 90-day program includes two years of weekly aftercare, and the 30-day program is followed by six weeks of weekly check-ins. The centre also mentions an intensive outpatient option for people who cannot commit to a residential stay.

Andy’s House offers withdrawal support, not a hospital detox unit. On arrival, staff run about an hour of assessments to judge whether you need medical attention, and if you do they take you to a doctor. People on methadone or Suboxone maintenance are not admitted, but the team can help arrange a medical detox from those medications first.

faqs.q: Is Andy’s House certified in Quebec?
faqs.a: Yes. Andy’s House says it is certified by Santé Québec and audited through Accreditation Canada. Its clinical staff also belong to Quebec professional orders, including the Ordre des psychologues du Québec.

faqs.q: Is treatment at Andy’s House in English or French?
faqs.a: Treatment at Andy’s House is in English. The admissions criteria ask that you can speak, write and understand English well enough to express yourself in groups. The centre does not say it offers a French-language program.

faqs.q: Where is Andy’s House and how do I get there?
faqs.a: Andy’s House is at 3360 Rue Notre-Dame in Lachine, on the Island of Montreal near Highway 20. It is about 20 minutes from downtown Montreal by car and 10 to 15 minutes from Dorval and the West Island. The house has no outside sign, so call the office before you come; Google lists it as open by appointment, Monday to Friday, 9 am to 6 pm.

faqs.q: Is Andy’s House private? Will RAMQ or my benefits cover it?
faqs.a: Yes, Andy’s House is a private centre, and recovery.com lists it as private pay with no insurers billed directly. RAMQ does not pay for a private residential stay. The centre suggests asking your insurance provider whether your plan covers part of the cost, and it offers financing through Medicard and Crédit Médical.
